_meta.note: Upgrade the MCP server to dual-stack the 2026-07-28 spec (the largest MCP revision since launch, published 2026-07-28) WITHOUT breaking today's hosts. Decisive investigation against the official Python SDK v2.0.0 (the executable spec) pinned the exact contract: the v2 client probes `server/discover` first and FALLS BACK to `initialize` for older servers — so `server/discover` is the negotiation pivot. DiscoverResult = {supportedVersions:[...], capabilities} with serverInfo in _meta (io.modelcontextprotocol/serverInfo); per-request protocol version travels in _meta (io.modelcontextprotocol/protocolVersion) or the mcp-protocol-version HTTP header; resultType/ttlMs/cacheScope are optional-with-defaults in the SDK models. Design: per-request MODERN detection — a modern request (2026 meta/header) gets server/discover + resultType + cache fields; an old request keeps TODAY'S byte-identical response (zero regression to Codex/Claude Code, which send `initialize`). Also fixes the version-echo bug (advertise versions we implement; stop echoing) and hardens the HTTP transport (validate Origin against DNS-rebinding; refuse non-loopback bind without --allow-remote). Interop is PROVEN by the real SDK v2 client over stdio as an on-demand tier (optional .[mcp-test] extra); the core stays stdlib-only and network never gates the suite. Out of scope (deprecated/optional in 2026): sampling, logging, roots, tasks/MRTR, subscriptions.

tasks.title: Author the 2026 wire-shape proof spec
tasks.description: Spec-first: write docs/howto/gate-examples/mcp-2026.sh (our own stdlib JSON-RPC client over stdio, deterministic — no SDK, no network). Assert: (1) server/discover returns supportedVersions containing both '2026-07-28' and '2025-06-18', a capabilities.tools object, and serverInfo under _meta['io.modelcontextprotocol/serverInfo']; (2) initialize with a supported protocolVersion echoes it; initialize with an UNSUPPORTED version (e.g. '2999-01-01') returns a version we actually implement ('2025-06-18'), NOT the bogus one (the echo bug is fixed); (3) a MODERN tools/call (request params._meta['io.modelcontextprotocol/protocolVersion']='2026-07-28') returns a result carrying resultType='complete', and a modern tools/list carries ttlMs + cacheScope; (4) an OLD tools/call (no modern _meta) returns a result with NO resultType/cache fields — byte-identical to today. Print MCP-2026-OK.

tasks.title: Implement dual-stack negotiation + server/discover + modern results
tasks.description: In py/src/heartbeat/mcp_server.py: define HANDSHAKE_VERSIONS ({'2025-06-18'}), MODERN_VERSIONS ({'2026-07-28'}), DISCOVER_VERSIONS (['2026-07-28','2025-06-18']). Fix `initialize` to return the requested version iff supported, else our latest handshake version (stop echoing arbitrary strings). Add a `server/discover` handler returning {supportedVersions: DISCOVER_VERSIONS, capabilities:{tools:{}}, _meta:{'io.modelcontextprotocol/serverInfo':{name,version}}}. Add _is_modern(msg) (checks params._meta protocol version). For a modern request, add resultType='complete' to tools/call + tools/list results and ttlMs(0)+cacheScope('private') to list; for an old request leave the response exactly as today. The server stays STATELESS (a cold tools/call with no prior initialize already works) and STDLIB-ONLY (pure dict work, no new imports).

tasks.title: Author the HTTP-security proof spec
tasks.description: Spec-first: extend docs/howto/gate-examples/mcp-http.sh with a security section (urllib over localhost, deterministic): (1) a POST with Origin: http://evil.example is rejected with HTTP 403 (DNS-rebinding defense); (2) a POST with no Origin (non-browser clients) and a POST with Origin http://localhost:<port> are accepted (200); (3) starting `hb mcp-serve --http --host 0.0.0.0` WITHOUT --allow-remote refuses to start (non-zero + a security message) while --host 127.0.0.1 (loopback) starts; (4) a modern POST carrying the mcp-protocol-version: 2026-07-28 header gets a resultType in its result (modern detection over HTTP), and the mcp-method/mcp-name headers are tolerated. Keep MCP-HTTP-OK; add MCP-HTTP-SECURE-OK.

tasks.title: Implement Origin validation + --allow-remote + header tolerance
tasks.description: In mcp_server.py serve_http + cli.py: reject a request whose Origin header is present and not loopback (localhost/127.0.0.1/[::1]) with 403 (no state touched). Add --allow-remote to the mcp-serve subparser; if --host is non-loopback and --allow-remote is not set, refuse to start with a clear security message and non-zero exit; print the security posture on start. Wire modern detection over HTTP via the mcp-protocol-version header (feed it into _is_modern's logic). Tolerate (ignore) mcp-method/mcp-name headers. Stay stdlib-only.
